name: publicWeb_resolveCustomDomain
description: Resolves a custom domain hostname (tier 3) to the kennel slug that should handle it. Called by the Next.js middleware for every request from an unrecognised hostname; the result is cached in-process. Only kennels whose KennelWebsite.Enabled = 1 and that are not deleted/removed resolve. Unauthenticated (PublicWebApi GET shim).

parameters.name: CustomDomain
parameters.description: Hostname without port (e.g. 'www.decisionhall.com'), exact match against HC.KennelWebsite.CustomDomain (unique where not NULL). No SQL default.
parameters.typeMismatch: KennelWebsite.CustomDomain is NVARCHAR(250); the parameter is NVARCHAR(253) (the DNS maximum). A hostname longer than the column simply matches nothing.

rowsets.name: ResolvedKennel
rowsets.description: Zero or one row (CustomDomain is unique). Zero rows → the shim returns 404.

columns.name: KennelSlug
columns.description: HC.Kennel.KennelUniqueShortName — the internal path segment to rewrite the request to

rowsets.name: ErrorEnvelope
rowsets.description: Instead of ResolvedKennel on a runtime error (CATCH). PublicWebApi logs it as 'HC6 Public Web Error: resolveCustomDomain' and returns 400.

codeSmells.detail: @CustomDomain (line 2) has no SQL default. A caller that omits it fails with 'expects parameter' before the SP runs: PublicWebApi's catch logs only a generic exception row and returns 500, and the SP's own graceful checks and error envelope never run.

codeSmells.issue: CATCH block does not log to HC.ErrorLog
codeSmells.detail: Lines 35-38 return { Success = 0, ErrorMessage } without an HC.ErrorLog row; PublicWebApi logs the envelope generically, without the hostname that failed.

breakingChangeRules: Never change the zero-row = no match contract — middleware depends on this
Never remove the kw.Enabled = 1 filter — routing disabled kennels would expose their content at their custom domain
